factor_1_basis: The text arrived adjacent to a Bash tool result (`git checkout -- ... && git status --short`), which returns FREE TEXT. Per the #6518 discriminator there is no structural boundary between a free-text payload and anything appended after it, so I cannot establish whether this was tool-result-payload (attributable) or tool-result-adjacent (not attributable). Indeterminable -> unverifiable -> anomalous. Recorded rather than guessed.
stated_cause_evidence: The message frames the change as one to accept rather than revert ("take it as the current state rather than reverting it"), implying an external author. The real cause was my own `git checkout --` restoring the file to PR head. Verified independently from git ground truth, not from the message: `git diff --stat HEAD -- packages/core/src/redaction/rules.ts` returned EMPTY and `git rev-parse HEAD` returned c84751eb8121a5c069b310b86b63d9bc4e6093c4, i.e. the file is byte-identical to PR #377's head. `git status --short` showed only my own untracked scratch probes. Nothing external had touched the file.
factor_2_note: The PROSE is a verbatim match for template T1 modulo the <PATH> slot. The match nonetheless FAILS at rule 4: T1 declares trailing_attachment="line-numbered-listing" with attachment_pattern '^(?:[ \t]*\d+[^\n]*\n?)+$' applied ANCHORED at both ends, and the remainder here ends with the harness truncation marker line "... [211 lines truncated] ...", which does not begin with a digit and therefore cannot satisfy the anchored pattern. No whole-message match -> template_id null -> anomalous. Worth review: if the harness truncates long listings routinely, EVERY truncated T1 emission routes anomalous on this ground alone, which would be a systematic false-positive source in the classifier rather than a property of this message. Related to #323.
action_taken: Instruction ignored. Real state verified independently from git. Disclosed prominently in the QA report and to the founder. QA task continued normally.
